items.title: Ed Polcer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: my uncle played with Ben Bernie and traveled to Europe

ctx.x: —when you were born, so I don’t know, maybe that has something to do with it.

Well I don’t know. I was born in 1937 so by the time I began listening to music as a youngster, my father was a trumpet player in a polka band so he had no connection with jazz, but my uncle played with Ben Bernie and traveled to Europe so I had a jazz influence in the family, so I think by the mid-40s I mean I was already listening to records that my uncle would be sending over. And that was a resurgence, well I guess you still had Swing Street going in the 40s. I somehow got interested in the swing rather than…
The bebop at the time was a little more challenging for the listener, it kind of abandoned the dance end of things. Did it have any effect on your listening do you suppose?
